segments.interpretation: The executable claim is a negative descriptive conditional-minus-whole-scope difference. Replenishment and demand are proposed explanations, not separately tested causal or order-book claims; no empirical success is asserted.
segments.text: Hypothesis: unusually intense aggressive buying that produces an intrabar rally but almost no retained gain in ETHUSDT reflects replenishing passive sell supply rather than latent bullish demand. Contrary to the standard intuition that high taker-buy participation and high turnover predict continuation, I hypothesize a lower subsequent one-hour ETH return after this failed buying impulse than across the whole eligible ETH scope. This is an original, untested development hypothesis, not evidence of profitability or a causal conclusion.

segments.interpretation: At signal coordinate s, lag-one trailing_median over 96 quote-volume arguments reads exactly s-900 through s-86400. The approved even-window median averages the two central sorted values. Every exact argument must be observed, finite, in interval and available; no missing argument shortens or shifts the window.
segments.text: Exact condition: let O_s, H_s, C_s, Q_s, and B_s be ETH open, high, close, quote volume, and taker quote volume for the signal bar. Let M_s be the ordinary median of quote volumes at the preceding 96 exact grid ends s-900k, k=1,...,96; for 96 observations use the arithmetic average of the two central sorted values. Require all 96 observations, without skipping or substitution.

segments.interpretation: P is exactly the conjunction of the four specified inclusive threshold requirements, with the retained-gain range represented by its inclusive lower and upper comparisons. Same-price-unit divisions produce ratios; the turnover multiplier preserves USDT.
segments.text: The condition is true exactly when B_s/Q_s >= 0.65, Q_s >= 2*M_s, H_s/O_s-1 >= 0.003, and 0 <= C_s/O_s-1 <= 0.0005.

These checks cover every required signal scalar and the complete median window. Finite execution inputs are required by row admission; invalid raw keyed bars project to null under the supplied definitions. V is true only when all specified completeness and validity requirements hold. False or unknown V produces an unknown condition through the enclosing guard, not a scope exclusion. segments.text: A 65% buy share represents materially one-sided aggressive flow; twice the preceding day's median turnover distinguishes a participation burst from ordinary noise; a 30-basis-point upward excursion with only zero to five basis points retained isolates failed upward progress. The 96-bar baseline spans one day without requiring an additional regime model. These are mechanism-motivated exploratory choices, not fitted thresholds.

segments.interpretation: At h=5 the future anchor is a=t+4500. Close lag one reads C_{t+3600}; open lag four reads O_{t+900}. Their ratio is dimensionless, ln is natural logarithm, and the multiplier expresses the dimensionless log change in basis points. The supplied positive_decimal price definitions and invalid-keyed-bar-to-null projection enforce finite positive observed prices; required missing, invalid or unavailable prices propagate missing, and nonfinite execution inputs fail admission. The exact-snapshot timing certificate implies close availability a and open availability a-2700. Thus, for an elapsed in-universe horizon, an inherited outcome cutoff min(as_of,end-1 second) cannot admit a dependency unavailable at the original min(a,end-1 second): both dependencies are already available by a, and the certificate rules out later recorded availability. At a=end the final close is unavailable by end-1 second; for later anchors its key is outside the interval. Hence near-end cases remain missing without adding an anchor-capped cutoff or changing the horizon. Required-inputs/1 does not demand an unused outcome-anchor container. The approved ln enclosure is propagated through means and their difference, without a midpoint decision or simple-return substitution.
segments.text: Outcome: choose positive integer h=5, so the outcome evaluation anchor is a=t+4500 seconds. Define Y_t=10000*ln(C_{t+3600}/O_{t+900}), using ETH bar-end keys. The denominator is the opening price of the bar spanning t to t+900; the numerator is the close of the bar ending t+3600. Thus Y describes the market's one-hour price change starting at decision t, expressed in log basis points. It is not a return from the stale signal close. At anchor a, the final close has its assumed 900-second publication delay satisfied. Both prices must be finite and positive, available by cutoff min(a, 2023-04-01T00:00:00Z minus one second), and have keys within the permitted interval. Near-end outcomes lacking these requirements remain missing; do not obtain April data or shorten the horizon. The future opening price is an outcome measurement, not information available to the condition or an assumed executable fill. Raw ETH prices have units USDT/ETH; only their ratios and Y are dimensionless.

segments.interpretation: Compute mean(Y|C=true,S=true,Y observed) minus mean(Y|S=true,Y observed), with equal decision-row weights, whole_scope comparator, negative direction and no nuisance fitting. The baseline retains both false and unknown conditions. Overlapping outcomes are not deduplicated or reweighted. A negative difference does not assert a negative conditional mean or independent observations.
segments.text: Comparison and weighting: the target descriptive contrast is the equal-decision-row mean Y among condition-true rows minus the equal-decision-row mean Y across the entire ETH decision grid with observed Y, including condition-false and condition-unknown rows. This intentionally uses the whole-scope benchmark, not a matched control or false-only group. The hypothesized contrast is negative. It need not imply that the conditional mean itself is negative. Overlapping hourly outcomes remain included with equal weight; they are not independent observations.

segments.interpretation: The exact composition is (V AND P) OR ((NOT V) AND unknown), beneath the signal lag, with identical V copies at /condition_ast/expression/arg/left/left and /condition_ast/expression/arg/right/left/arg. For V=true it equals P; for V=false or unknown it is unknown, even if P is false. Consequently a missing H_s, C_s or median argument cannot be masked by a false threshold or another invalid check. The literal unknown is not a missing market observation. The actual predicate-to-validity derivation, rather than guard recognition alone, is provided above for independent review.
segments.text: Missingness: if any required condition input or baseline observation is absent, null, unavailable, invalid under the stated checks, or outside the interval, label the condition unknown rather than false; use complete-condition evaluation rather than inferring false from a partial conjunction. Never forward-fill.

A false V identifies a stated validity failure; an unknown V is not automatically classified as an invalid value. Missing values/features and pre-universe dependencies remain separately observable neutral categories. Literal null and unused coordinates are not absent market inputs. Counts overlap and count a row once per category. An empty observed conditional group yields an undefined contrast, not zero. Diagnostic or numerical resource exhaustion must be reported as incomplete with RESOURCE_STOP and processed/unprocessed counts; no completed report or measured result is claimed here.
segments.text: Condition-unknown rows stay in scope and enter the whole-scope outcome mean when Y is observed, but never enter the conditional mean. Missing Y is excluded from either mean, with separate counts retained for boundary censoring, absent rows, invalid values, unavailable data, missing warmup, and condition unknown. An empty conditional group leaves the contrast undefined. These rules make the descriptive estimand an observed-outcome contrast, with selection limitations rather than an implied result for missing outcomes.
